assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law and finance created a large empirical and conceptual research program on how legal institutions and investor protection shape financial development, ownership structure and growth. It reaches corporate finance, comparative institutions and development. The influence is very broad and has lasted.
assessment.attribution: The core 1990s papers are jointly authored by La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny. A three-person limit forces a choice. Shleifer, La Porta and Lopez-de-Silanes are the most plausible trio from my reading of the literature. Vishny's contribution is substantial, so the exclusion is a real cost.
assessment.maturity: The work is about 25-30 years old and has been widely replicated, extended and critiqued. Its influence on policy and measurement, such as the Doing Business-style indicators, is well documented.
uncertainties: Legal-origin causal claims and the coding of the original anti-director index have been criticised.
Some of the later institutional work is disputed.
The fourth-person exclusion problem remains.
I rely on my own recollection of the literature and have not verified sources independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm-heterogeneity trade models changed how trade is analysed. They explain exporter selection, intra-industry reallocation and the gains from trade with micro-level facts. They are now the workhorse framework in international trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution, and Helpman is a leading architect of the broader new trade theory and heterogeneous-firm extensions. Redding is an important contributor to quantitative and spatial extensions but is arguably later or more derivative. Krugman has already been recognised for the earlier new trade theory.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of confirmation across many countries and datasets. The framework is standard in graduate teaching and policy modelling.
uncertainties: The weight of Helpman against other trade candidates, including B041 and the Bernard-Jensen empirical work not listed here.
Priority questions around related heterogeneous-firm work.
Whether the committee prefers to recognise trade through a different combination.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: These authors built modern political economics. They gave a rigorous, empirically testable account of how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and development outcomes. The field now connects theory with data and is influential in macro, public and development economics.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are closely linked through their joint program and book. Besley's work on state capacity, accountability and political agency is closely related and independently strong. The trio is coherent, though other contributors to political economy are omitted.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of development, with extensive empirical testing and a large following. The work is clearly mature.
uncertainties: Some empirical claims on constitutional effects face identification challenges.
The Acemoglu-Johnson-Robinson prize in 2024 overlaps thematically on institutions, so the committee may see less urgency.
Persson's links to the Swedish committee environment would be a disclosed conflict, not adjudicated here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. With the financial accelerator work, it provides the standard theory of credit cycles and a basis for post-2008 macro-financial modelling. Policy relevance is high.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore have the clearest claim, since the credit-cycles paper is jointly theirs. Gertler is credited for the financial accelerator and later macro-finance work. Bernanke, who shares the accelerator lineage, was already recognised in 2022. Gilchrist is a significant but narrower contributor.
assessment.maturity: The theory has been tested and extended for almost three decades, and the 2008 crisis strongly increased its relevance. Direct causal evidence on the amplification mechanism is more mixed.
uncertainties: How much weight the committee gives Gertler against Bernanke's earlier recognition.
Mostly theoretical and calibrated support for the quantitative amplification claims.
The overlap with the Diamond-Dybvig and Bernanke prize in 2022.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework underpin modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice. The Taylor rule, Calvo pricing and the Woodford synthesis are widely used in practice.
assessment.attribution: This candidate lists eight names, which shows a diffuse authorship. Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (policy rules and staggered contracts) and Woodford (the microfounded synthesis) are conceptually distinct core contributions. Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and others are important but later or more applied. Any trio omits major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature. The framework has shaped policy for 30 years, although the 2008 crisis and the 2021-23 inflation episode put the framework under scrutiny.
uncertainties: The attribution boundary is large and contested.
Previous recognition of related macro work, such as Lucas, Kydland-Prescott, Sargent-Sims and Phelps-Taylor lineages, may lower the committee's interest.
The inflation episode has revived debate on how well the model holds up.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run top-income series built from tax data transformed the measurement of inequality and shifted the policy debate. They created a data infrastructure, the World Inequality Database, that is widely used.
assessment.attribution: Piketty-Saez (2003) is the foundational joint paper. Zucman has an important contribution on offshore wealth and wealth distribution but is much more junior. Atkinson, who is deceased, is not listed. Saez also appears in B007, which raises a possible double-counting issue.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years of use. Fundamental measurement results have been replicated, but some findings, such as post-tax inequality trends, are disputed.
uncertainties: Methodological critiques of the wealth and income allocation.
Weight of measurement and data work against theory.
Possible concerns over policy advocacy and the theoretical claims in the capital-return arguments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work clarified how technology, tasks and trade exposure reshape labour demand, polarization and local labour markets. The China-shock papers are among the most influential empirical papers in recent decades and altered trade-policy debate. The task-based approach is a lasting framework.
assessment.attribution: The task framework runs through Autor with Levy, Murnane and Katz. The China shock is Autor-Dorn-Hanson. Katz is also credited for related labour work. A trio of Autor, Hanson and Dorn fits the China-shock lineage best. The task-model contribution is split with others and with Acemoglu, who is already a laureate.
assessment.maturity: Roughly 10-20 years of work. The effects have been widely replicated and debated. Long-run adjustment and welfare conclusions are still being refined.
uncertainties: Identification of the shift-share exposure measures has been debated.
Long-run effects of the China shock are still evolving.
Overlap with Acemoglu's recent recognition for technology and inequality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Duffie's work on reduced-form credit-risk pricing, term-structure models and OTC market structure, along with search-based models of OTC markets and liquidity, shaped asset-pricing theory and post-crisis market regulation. The influence on practice is considerable, including on clearing and derivatives policy.
assessment.attribution: Duffie is the dominant name, with foundational contributions in credit risk and affine models, plus OTC search theory with Duffie-Garleanu-Pedersen. Pedersen and Garleanu are credited for the OTC and liquidity work. Joint authorship makes this a less clean fit than a single-contribution candidate. The finance literature has several adjacent sets of leading contributors, for example Brunnermeier and Pedersen, B022, whose work overlaps.
assessment.maturity: The credit-risk and affine work is more than 25 years old and fully mature. The OTC search models are about 20 years old and have been tested empirically.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a single coherent discovery or as separate contributions.
Recent finance prizes, 2013 and 2022, may weigh against further finance recognition.
Possible overlap with other asset-pricing candidates such as B022.
My own field proximity may bias my sense of its importance.
